commercial_hypothesis: Offline premium Windows. Target at least NOK 20,000 cash profit per game, before owner wage/personal tax. Only consider several games after actual results prove worthwhile. Price, production budget and sales unvalidated; no spending authorized.
evidence_limits: Desk research. No playable prototype, paid demand for this exact hook, measured production speed, or owner acceptance. Working label, not cleared final title.
title: Night Inspection — research label
hook: Inspect a familiar room against its reference state, detect the impossible change and decide whether to clear it for the next occupant.
audience: Players of short atmospheric anomaly and inspection horror.
core_loop: Learn the reference room; inspect one finite event; choose clear or reject; advance through a short shift; reach one ending.

evidence.claim: The Cabin Factory developer reports over 50,000 copies in five days on 2024-12-18. Development duration and platform split not established.
Telephone Call has weak filtered Steam review response in the run snapshot, without a revenue claim.

risks: Close established competition; distinguishing hook unvalidated.
Custom monsters, chase AI, mirrors or branching lore destroy the few-day envelope.
Short duration and ambiguous event rules can frustrate buyers and create refunds.
next_test: If preferred, make one room with three test events and unambiguous inspect/clear decisions. Judge readability and tension in actual play before authoring up to twelve finite events.
decision_reason: Retained 3D alternative, ranked behind active incremental and conditional hidden-object for workload. Not a resumption of the parked FPS or a selected game.
